quiz_title: 🤖 PicToBlox Challenge 5: Scoreboards, Pen Drawings & Functions

questions.question: What is a Variable in PicToBlox programming?
options: A color option for drawing backdrops
A named box in the computer memory used to store values (like scores or speed) that can change
A button to export game files
An animal sprite in the library
questions.explanation: Spot on! Variables act as data containers, holding values like player scores, health counters, or speeds that update during gameplay.

questions.question: If you want to add 1 point to a player's score every time a basketball successfully hits the net, which block should you snap in?
questions.explanation: Correct! The 'change variable by' block increases or decreases the stored value by the amount specified (e.g. +1 for adding points).

questions.question: Which block from the Pen extension is used to start drawing lines on the stage canvas as your sprite moves?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'pen down' block places the virtual pen onto the canvas, trailing lines wherever the sprite travels.

questions.question: Why do we create custom blocks using the 'My Blocks' feature in PicToBlox?
options: To download sounds from the web
To group and repeat a bundle of blocks under a single name, reducing code repetition and making scripts neat
To change the language of the application
To speed up the computer keyboard
questions.explanation: Great! Custom 'My Blocks' act like procedures or functions, letting us package a long series of drawing or motion blocks into one single reusable block.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to set a variable named 'Score' to 0 when the green flag is clicked.
questions.task_hint: Write: when green flag clicked -> set Score to 0
questions.explanation: Perfect! Setting your score variables to 0 at game startup is called initializing variables, ensuring players start fresh.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to put the Pen down, move 100 steps, and lift the Pen up.
questions.task_hint: Write: pen down -> move 100 steps -> pen up
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Snap these three blocks in sequence to draw a clean line segment of exactly 100 pixels on the stage!
